text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1% today to $131.83, extending a two-week slide of nearly 3%. The stock has tumbled sharply since September 15th amid escalating Middle East tensions—Iran has closed the Strait of Hormuz, the Houthis are intensifying attacks on shipping, and there are reports of strikes near Saudi Arabia's main airport. Despite these geopolitical flashpoints that normally support oil prices, the market appears to be pricing in that disruptions will be contained; the fact that Saudi pipeline damage was seen as "less disruptive than feared" suggests traders don't yet expect a sustained supply shock that would lift energy stocks.

The disconnect between rising geopolitical risk and falling oil stocks hints at deeper economic concern. Record diesel prices are already hitting transportation hard, and if energy costs stay elevated, demand could weaken across the broader economy—which would pressure both crude prices and refiner margins over time. In this environment, the stock may be caught between fear of supply disruption (bullish for prices) and fear of demand destruction (bearish for volumes and profitability).
